verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.114
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 4.114

verses.pali: 12. Kesivagga
verses.english: 12. With Kesi

verses.pali: Nāgasutta
verses.english: A Royal Elephant

verses.pali: “Catūhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato rañño nāgo rājāraho hoti rājabhoggo, rañño aṅganteva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
verses.english: “Mendicants, a royal bull elephant with four factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and is reckoned a factor of kingship.

verses.pali: Katamehi catūhi?
verses.english: What four?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo sotā ca hoti, hantā ca, khantā ca, gantā ca.
verses.english: A royal bull elephant listens, destroys, endures, and goes fast.

verses.pali: Kathañca, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo sotā hoti?
verses.english: And how does a royal bull elephant listen?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo yamenaṁ hatthidammasārathi kāraṇaṁ kāreti—
verses.english: It’s when a royal bull elephant pays attention, applies the mind, concentrates wholeheartedly, and actively listens to whatever task the elephant trainer has it do,

verses.pali: yadi vā katapubbaṁ yadi vā akatapubbaṁ—
verses.english: whether or not it has done it before.

verses.pali: taṁ aṭṭhiṁ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasoto suṇāti.
Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo sotā hoti.
verses.english: That’s how a royal bull elephant listens.

verses.pali: Kathañca, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo hantā hoti?
verses.english: And how does a royal bull elephant destroy?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo saṅgāmagato hatthimpi hanati, hatthāruhampi hanati, assampi hanati, assāruhampi hanati, rathampi hanati, rathikampi hanati, pattikampi hanati.
verses.english: It’s when a royal bull elephant in battle destroys elephants with their riders, horses with their riders, chariots and charioteers, and foot soldiers.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo hantā hoti.
verses.english: That’s how a royal bull elephant destroys.

verses.pali: Kathañca, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo khantā hoti?
verses.english: And how does a royal bull elephant endure?

verses.pali: Idha bhikkhave, rañño nāgo saṅgāmagato khamo hoti sattippahārānaṁ asippahārānaṁ usuppahārānaṁ pharasuppahārānaṁ bheripaṇavasaṅkhatiṇavaninnādasaddānaṁ.
verses.english: It’s when a royal bull elephant in battle endures being struck by spears, swords, arrows, and axes; it endures the thunder of the drums, kettledrums, horns, and cymbals.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo khantā hoti.
verses.english: That’s how a royal bull elephant endures.

verses.pali: Kathañca, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo gantā hoti?
verses.english: And how does a royal bull elephant go fast?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo yamenaṁ hatthidammasārathi disaṁ peseti—
verses.english: It’s when a royal bull elephant swiftly goes in whatever direction the elephant trainer sends it,

verses.pali: yadi vā gatapubbaṁ yadi vā agatapubbaṁ—
verses.english: whether or not it has been there before.

verses.pali: taṁ khippameva gantā hoti.
Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo gantā hoti.
verses.english: That’s how a royal bull elephant goes fast.

verses.pali: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi aṅgehi samannāgato rañño nāgo rājāraho hoti rājabhoggo, rañño aṅganteva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
verses.english: A royal bull elephant with four factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and is reckoned a factor of kingship.

verses.pali: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
verses.english: In the same way, a mendicant with four qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.

verses.pali: Katamehi catūhi?
verses.english: What four?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sotā ca hoti, hantā ca, khantā ca, gantā ca.
verses.english: A mendicant listens, destroys, endures, and goes fast.

verses.pali: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sotā hoti?
verses.english: And how does a mendicant listen?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye desiyamāne aṭṭhiṁ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasoto dhammaṁ suṇāti.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant pays attention, applies the mind, concentrates wholeheartedly, and actively listens when the teaching and training proclaimed by a Realized One is being taught.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sotā hoti.
verses.english: That’s how a mendicant listens.

verses.pali: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu hantā hoti?
verses.english: And how does a mendicant destroy?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu uppannaṁ kāmavitakkaṁ nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti hanati byantīkaroti anabhāvaṁ gameti, uppannaṁ byāpādavitakkaṁ …pe… uppannaṁ vihiṁsāvitakkaṁ …pe… uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti hanati byantīkaroti anabhāvaṁ gameti.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t tolerate a sensual, malicious, or cruel thought. They don’t tolerate any bad, unskillful qualities that have arisen, but give them up, get rid of them, eliminate them, and obliterate them.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu hantā hoti.
verses.english: That’s how a mendicant destroys.

verses.pali: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu khantā hoti?
verses.english: And how does a mendicant endure?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu khamo hoti sītassa uṇhassa jighacchāya pipāsāya, ḍaṁsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassānaṁ duruttānaṁ durāgatānaṁ vacanapathānaṁ uppannānaṁ sārīrikānaṁ vedanānaṁ dukkhānaṁ tibbānaṁ kharānaṁ kaṭukānaṁ asātānaṁ amanāpānaṁ pāṇaharānaṁ adhivāsakajātiko hoti.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant endures cold, heat, hunger, and thirst; the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and reptiles; rude and unwelcome criticism; and they put up with physical pain—sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, disagreeable, and life-threatening.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu khantā hoti.
verses.english: That’s how a mendicant endures.

verses.pali: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu gantā hoti?
verses.english: And how does a mendicant go fast?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yāyaṁ disā agatapubbā iminā dīghena addhunā yadidaṁ sabbasaṅkhārasamatho sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggo taṇhākkhayo virāgo nirodho nibbānaṁ, taṁ khippaññeva gantā hoti.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant swiftly goes in the direction they’ve never gone before in all this long time; that is, the stilling of all activities, the letting go of all attachments, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishment.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu gantā hoti.
verses.english: That’s how a mendicant goes fast.

verses.pali: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
verses.english: A mendicant with these four qualities … is the supreme field of merit for the world.”

verses.pali: Catutthaṁ.
